method: One fresh agent session per task drives Atelier, loading the atelier-sprite skill and working only through Atelier's tools in its own isolated store. Every model draws the same ten tasks from identical frozen briefs (showcase/tasks/*.txt). The Anthropic models run in headless Claude Code (claude -p) with customizations and MCP servers disabled and only the Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, and Grep tools available; the OpenAI models run in Codex. All models run at xhigh reasoning effort. For Claude Code, xhigh is the level requested on the command line, and each assistant turn was checked for the requested model. For Codex, each session turn was checked for the requested model and reasoning effort. A CLI wrapper records every Atelier call, including failed calls and excluding harness export and verification. Tokens are cumulative input plus output from the session’s reported usage, including cached input and, for Claude Code, cache writes. The manifest also records the separate token-usage fields. Durations are omitted: agents ran concurrently, so wall-clock is queueing, not work. Interrupted sessions were resumed with their original stores and artwork. This includes GPT-6.2 Sol’s torch and GPT-6.2 Astra’s slash and torch. Five Claude Code sessions (sonnet-5-xhigh/potion, sonnet-5-xhigh/slash, opus-4.8-xhigh/slash, opus-5-xhigh/person, opus-5-xhigh/potion) were killed by a host restart before reporting usage; their input tokens are summed from per-message usage and their output tokens cover only the resumed invocation, so those totals slightly undercount. The same restart corrupted a few bytes of the sonnet-5-xhigh/potion call log, so its call count may be short by one. The Claude recipes were later re-recorded, first using newer tool features (cropped grids, replace mode, frame ranges, and hex colours) and then as the exact call log, one JSON line per call. Each still rebuilds its GIF byte for byte, but a recipe can hold fewer calls than the count recorded for its run.
server: The 20 GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra runs used the repository build at a3ddd6d6b75ddbad6118f464b77e476430045790 (atelier 0.2.0, 27-tool surface) with codex-cli 0.170.0. The 80 Anthropic runs used one binary built from the repository at ac90b5d6f096876776da670e7cd868c40012d354 (reported version 0.1.0, 26-tool surface) with Claude Code 2.1.295 or 2.1.296. Every run used isolated CLI dispatch with one store per task.
verified: Every GIF has 10 frames at 100 ms each and a transparent background. The canvas is 32×32 (48×48 for beam) at scale 4, within the requested colour limits. CI replays all 100 committed recipes through the repository build and requires the exported GIFs to match byte for byte.
